summary: Defines an XML schema for the vCard data format, so contact information can be represented in XML.

eli5.summary: A vCard is a digital business card written in a plain-text style. This gives the same card in XML, another way of writing information, which some programs prefer.

questions: what is the difference between vcard and xcard
how to convert vcard to xml
subtitle: The same contact card as vCard, written in XML so programs with an XML engine can reuse it.

tldr.problem: vCard is a text-based format for contact information, but some environments already have an XML engine and would rather not write a separate vCard parser.
tldr.mechanism: xCard maps vCard properties, parameters and value types to XML elements, using a RELAX NG schema and a 1-to-1 mapping with the original format.
tldr.outcome: Cards can be converted between vCard and xCard in both directions, with rules for extensions and unrecognized data.

today: RFC 6351 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 6868. No RFC obsoleting it is listed in the metadata.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
vCard (RFC 6350) is a text-based data format for representing and exchanging information about individuals and other entities. RFC 6351 defines xCard, an XML representation of it.

The underlying data structure is exactly the same, giving a 1-to-1 mapping between the original vCard format and the XML. The RFC says the XML form may be preferred where an XML engine is readily available and can be reused instead of writing a standalone vCard parser.

The RFC also notes that earlier work on an XML format for vCard was started in 1998 by Frank Dawson, and that it 'did not take over the world'. The schema is written in the RELAX NG language and given in Appendix A.
sections.eli5: It is the same address card, just written down in a different style. Programs that already understand that style do not need to learn a new one.

sections.title: How vCard Maps to XML
sections.content:
The general idea is to map vCard parameters, properties and value types to XML elements. The FN property becomes an fn element, which contains a text element holding the value.

Parameters are elements too, placed inside a parameters element within the property. A parameter that takes a list of values is repeated, once per value. Properties with structured values, such as N, become element trees with names like surname and given; those names have no vCard equivalent because plain vCard identifies them by position.

The root is a vcards element holding one or more vcard elements, each one a full card. The root MUST be present even for a single card. The vCard group construct becomes a group element whose name attribute holds the group name.

Line folding is not an issue in XML, so the mapping from vCard is done after unfolding, and the mapping back is done before folding.
sections.eli5: Each part of the card gets its own labelled box. A phone number goes in a box marked tel, a name in a box marked fn, and the boxes nest inside a box for the whole card.

sections.title: An Example Card
sections.content:
The RFC gives the author's own card as an example. It lives in the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:vcard-4.0 and holds a name with several suffixes, a birthday, an anniversary, two languages with preference values, an organization, an address, two telephone numbers, an email address, a geographic location, a key, a time zone and a URL.

A smaller example shows a TYPE parameter on a TEL property: the type element sits in parameters, and it holds one text element for each value, such as voice and video. The telephone number itself goes in a uri element.
sections.eli5: The example is one full business card, with name, phone numbers and address, each in its own labelled box.

sections.title: Extensions and Limitations
sections.content:
vCard can be extended with new properties, parameters, data types and values registered with IANA. The RFC expects such extensions to also define extensions to the XML format. New XML property and parameter element names MUST be lower-case so that round-tripping between XML and plain-text vCard works.

Unregistered X- and VND-...- extensions become elements starting with x- and vnd-...-. For extensions with no plain-text vCard equivalent, using XML namespaces is RECOMMENDED.

A parser MUST ignore XML elements and attributes whose expanded name it does not recognize, and must ignore unrecognized processing instructions. The vCard VERSION property does not exist in XML; the version number in the core namespace identifier plays that role, and vCard revisions will use a different namespace.

The schema does not check how many times a property may appear. The cardinalities from RFC 6350 still MUST be respected. Some constructs, such as value enumerations in type parameters, have an ordering constraint in XML that must be respected, although conversion to or from plain vCard MAY reorder them.
sections.eli5: You can add your own boxes to the card, as long as they have their own clearly marked labels. A program that does not know a box just skips it.

sections.title: Converting Between vCard and xCard
sections.content:
A converter may meet properties or parameters it does not recognize, yet it must preserve their values. From vCard to xCard, a property with no VALUE parameter and an unknown default type is converted using the unknown element, holding the unprocessed text. Unrecognized parameters likewise use unknown, treated as text. The content of XML properties is copied as is. Names become lower-case, and value escaping and parameter quoting are undone.

From xCard to vCard, known properties use their plain-text form (for example adr becomes the ADR property). Otherwise the name comes from the element name, parameters from parameters and content from the value element, and unrecognized extra elements and attributes are dropped. The RFC therefore RECOMMENDS keeping extensions at the property level so that round trips lose nothing. Properties in other namespaces are wrapped inside an XML property. Names become upper-case, and escaping and quoting are applied again.
sections.eli5: Switching between the two styles is like translating a letter. Words the translator does not know are carried across unchanged, so nothing gets lost.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: All the security considerations of plain vCard (RFC 6350) also apply to xCard. The RFC adds that XML Signature and XML Encryption can be used with xCard to provide authentication and confidentiality.
sections.eli5: The same safety rules as the normal card apply. XML also has tools to sign a card to prove who made it, or to lock it so only the right person can read it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC registers the XML namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:vcard-4.0, with the IESG as registrant contact.

It also registers the media type application/vcard+xml. The optional charset parameter is as defined for application/xml, and using utf-8 is 'STRONGLY RECOMMENDED'. The registration says applications that use the text/vcard media type can use this as an alternative, and that XML data should use .xml as the file extension. The change controller is the IETF.
sections.eli5: The RFC puts the format's name and its file type on the official list so everyone calls it the same thing.
